summary: Two 1873 range lights on the Merrimac River at Newburyport. The rear brick tower stands privately on Water Street; the front light moved in 1964 onto Coast Guard grounds.

structures.type: conical iron tower, raised 1901 with a wooden top
structures.status: standing, moved 1964 onto Coast Guard grounds
structures.note: The 1873 Board figure, as LighthouseFriends prints it, was 14 ft 6 in (about 4.4 m); the National Register nomination (recorded 1981) gives a 35-foot frame.
The 1873 Board figure, as LighthouseFriends prints it, was 32 ft; the nomination gives 53 ft.

access.note: Front light on Coast Guard grounds, grounds and tower closed. Rear light privately owned and not open to the public; dinners by advance reservation through the Lighthouse Preservation Society.

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard (front light); private owner (rear light)

events.note: Front and rear range towers built on Bayley's Wharf and Water Street sites
Lighted June 1, 1873, per the Board's record as LighthouseFriends prints it
Front light raised eleven feet with a wooden top; rear tower extended nine feet
Inspector Wilson W. Buchanan recommended replacing the keeper with a laborer in charge at $20 a month
Rear light candlepower changed from 2000 to 690 and the illuminant from coal gas to electricity (nomination)
Keeper's post discontinued 15 April 1933 after the lights were electrified
Front range tower moved from Bayley's Wharf onto Coast Guard property
Rear brick tower sold out of federal ownership (nomination gives 1964; LighthouseFriends says soon after 1961)
Merrimac River Coast Guard Station built next to the front light
Severe fire damage to the front light (LighthouseFriends says 1990s; a photo caption gives 1990)
Rear tower repainted, lantern room made over, heat pump installed for year-round dining

corrections.why: 4.5 m matches the 1873 iron base (14 ft 6 in, as LighthouseFriends prints the Board's 1873 description). The National Register nomination (recorded 1981) describes a 35-foot frame after the 1901 extension, about 10.7 m. The record should give the current height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Board's 1873 figure was 14 ft 6 in; the 1901 wooden top brought the tower to about 35 ft, which the National Register nomination (recorded 1981) gives. The two figures are for different dates.

LighthouseFriends and Weiss give 1788 for the Plum Island lights; Putnam gives 1789. Those lights are a different station (us-ma-newburyport-harbor, Newburyport Harbor Light) and are not this record's built date.

notes_for_editor: Keeper roster: the USLHS archive gives the same five stints for both the rear and the front light (showPeople/9417 and /2850); the same men may have tended both, but no source says so, and the story says only what the archive shows. George W. Stickney's first name is from the archive; LighthouseFriends gives George Stickney. Height disagreements: the 1873 Board figures (front 14 ft 6 in, rear 32 ft, both as LighthouseFriends prints them) do not match the National Register nomination (recorded 1981) (front 35 ft, rear 53 ft); the rear figures also do not reconcile with the 1901 nine-foot extension, which would give about 41 ft. The USLHS front-light page gives a height of 58 ft and a 53 ft tower height and labels the tower 'square hourglass (rear range)'; treated as unreliable. Rear tower shape: LighthouseFriends says pyramidal in 1873; the nomination says square. Focal height 17.7 m in the record has no source in the corpus; the 1873 focal planes (25 ft front, 47 ft rear) are in the LighthouseFriends quote of the Board. Storm of 1 October 1894: the Board's 'Salisbury Beach range (front) light' is named as at 'entrance to Newburyport Harbor'; the story does not connect it to the Water Street pair, and the editor should decide whether it is the same light. The 1891 Board list gives a reflector light for 'Newburyport Harbor Range (front)', which may be this light; the year (1890) is clear, the day is not read from OCR. The 1873 Board description and the 1872 appropriation are quoted by LighthouseFriends; the local corpus of Board reports starts in 1891, so these were not checked against primary text. The 1910 inspection report is also quoted only by LighthouseFriends. Johnson 1889 passage: page not located in the local index; the citation has no page. Putnam 'north side of the river' phrase: OCR text reads 'aye' before it; quoted only from 'at present on the north side of the river'. Newspapers: three Chronicling America searches (a station-name search 1873-1961, a 'range light' search for 1894-95, and a 'range lights' search for 1900-1933) returned no hits or no output, and one keeper-name search timed out; no newspaper source is used. Quotes from the NRHP forms are limited to unspaced OCR text; the forms have spaced letters elsewhere. The 1964 buyer of the rear tower is not named (a private owner, not a current resident). LighthouseFriends' account of the keeper's death gives a medical cause; it is left out. Plum Island 'Newburyport Harbor Light' is a separate station (us-ma-newburyport-harbor) and must not be merged here. The NRHP 87000887 and 87001486 listing dates were not verified; the record's 1987 nrhp_listed event is the NRHP number year. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the two National Register forms were recorded in 1981 (front September 1981, rear June 1981); 1987 is the listing year, so the story no longer calls them the 1987 nomination. The Board's 1891 reflector-light entry moved from the storms section to Building the light; it is not a storm. The story no longer says the front light was on Water Street (that is the rear light) and no longer places the Water Street pair on the river's north side, which no source says. The Barrett 'family kept the lights' generalisation is replaced by the roster span (1886 to 1933, with Hunt 1889 to 1893 between). Still open: the Johnson 1889 page (modernlighthous01boargoog has no page index in the corpus, so the footnote gives no page); the 1895 Board page for the Salisbury Beach entry (annualreportlig00boargoog has no page index); the 1891 day of the reflector light, which the OCR does not give.
